structured_output.question: E000 shows the template is a trivial stub (1.2% accuracy, 0.1 s), not a 50–70 s baseline, so H2.1.1's premise is wrong. The first real recipe will be built from scratch, and the decision that matters most is which architecture and epoch budget to start from. Question: what published fast-training recipes reach about 75% top-1 on CIFAR-100 from scratch in the fewest epochs or least wall-clock time? For whitened or airbench-style CNNs versus ResNet-18-class nets, how do the accuracy-vs-epoch curve, network width, and regularization strength (label smoothing, cutout, translate) trade off in the short, under-fitting regime of fewer than about 15 epochs? This tests H1.1/H1.1.2, H1.2 and H4.1.
queries: fast training CIFAR-100 few epochs speedrun
budgeted training learning rate schedule short epochs
label smoothing cutout underfitting short training budget
ResNet-18 CIFAR-100 single GPU minutes 75% accuracy
progressive resizing low resolution early epochs CNN training speed
rubric: Reports CIFAR-100 (or CIFAR-10 with a transferable ablation) accuracy as a function of epoch count or wall-clock time under a short budget (about 30 epochs or fewer)
Trains from scratch on a single GPU with no pretrained weights or extra data, and gives the architecture, width, optimizer and schedule in enough detail to reproduce
Ablates at least one lever in our tree: whitening or dirac init, network width or depth, augmentation or label-smoothing strength, LR schedule shape, progressive resizing, or data filtering
Gives accuracy numbers near the 70–80% CIFAR-100 range, or explicit time-to-accuracy figures
exclude: pretrained weights, ImageNet pretraining, transfer learning, distillation from pretrained teachers
external or synthetic extra training data (e.g., 80M Tiny Images, diffusion-generated data)
test-time augmentation or any use of the test set during training or tuning
multi-GPU or TPU large-batch distributed training results with no single-GPU applicability
long-schedule (200+ epoch) SOTA accuracy papers with no short-budget results
vision transformers trained for hundreds of epochs
